title: How Much Fiber in an Orange? 3.1g per Medium
description: Orange: about 3.1 g of fiber per 1 medium (11% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in an orange?

answer.note: USDA FoodData Central, Oranges, raw, all commercial varieties

intro: Orange ranks #9 of 15 fruits on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in orange by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in an orange?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists oranges, raw, all commercial varieties at 2.4 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 medium; 131 g) therefore has about 3.1 g of fiber and 62 calories. That is 11% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 13% of a 25 g day and 8% of a 38 g day.
A whole orange gives a few grams of fiber, mostly from the membranes and pith. Juicing leaves almost all of that behind, which is why the juice row in the table is close to zero.

sections.heading: Whole orange vs orange juice
paragraphs: A cup of orange juice takes two to three oranges to make but keeps very little of their fiber. Even “pulp” juice adds only a small amount. Eating the orange is the version that counts for fiber.
Mandarins and clementines are smaller, so expect less fiber per piece than a navel orange.

sections.heading: How orange compares with other fruits
paragraphs: Of the 15 fruits on this site, orange ranks #9 for fiber per typical serving and #6 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 5.1 g of fiber per 100 calories, a high ratio: you get a lot of fiber for the calories.

Close neighbors by serving: [banana](/fiber-in-banana) at 3.1 g (1 medium (7–8")); [guava](/fiber-in-guava) at 3 g (1 fruit); [prunes](/fiber-in-prunes) at 3.4 g (5 prunes). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), orange is #23 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding orange to your day
paragraphs: Keep whole oranges or clementines as a grab-and-go snack, or add segments to a salad with beans and greens.

Example: 1 orange, 1 oz almonds. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 6.6 g of fiber, with 3.1 g from the orange. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of orange?
faqs.a: 2.4 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Oranges, raw, all commercial varieties). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in orange (1 cup sections)?
faqs.a: About 4.3 g, for 180 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.
Very little. USDA lists about 0.5 g in a cup of fresh juice, compared with about 3 g in one medium orange.

faqs.q: Should I eat the white pith?
faqs.a: If you like it, yes. The pith and membranes are where much of an orange’s fiber sits.
